findings.evidence: The finding is confirmed and refined. backend/main.py:3036-3038 unconditionally calls initialize_state_db(state.db) before HumanMemoryHostService composition; backend/deskpet/memory/session_db.py:260-265 independently calls the same legacy initializer; HumanMemoryProgramStore.initialize_subject() only later calls initialize_human_memory_program_state_db(). On a missing database, the first legacy initializer therefore creates v34 without the human-memory bootstrap marker, after which human initialization rejects it as legacy. The plan must freeze this pre-migration dispatch before any state.db opener, SessionDB.initialize(), MemoryManager, provider, worker, API, backup, or writable SQLite connection: (1) acquire one startup epoch-decision lock and inspect read-only; (2) FRESH is only the approved fresh-prototype userdata lane plus an absent state.db, a zero-byte file, or valid SQLite user_version=0 with no non-SQLite user tables and no epoch marker; select HUMAN, immediately call initialize_human_memory_program_state_db(), durably claim human-memory-v1 before base migrations, and enable HumanMemoryHostService by default without a feature flag; (3) HUMAN-RESUME is a valid human_memory_program_bootstrap marker with user_version 0..42, including an interrupted base migration, or a fully valid recognized v35..v42 marker chain; select the human initializer and resume the exact chain, with valid v39-v41 treated as resumable partial S4 states rather than future or legacy; (4) LEGACY is an existing valid legacy database without a human bootstrap/marker, normally user_version 1..34; select only the unchanged explicit legacy composition, never apply v35-v42, never construct or lazily initialize HumanMemoryHostService, and return human_memory_program_legacy_database_unsupported from every human-memory endpoint; (5) INVALID is user_version=0 with legacy/user tables, v35..v42 without the required bootstrap/marker chain, mixed/checksum-invalid markers, or corrupt/ambiguous format; fail closed before either migrator or any business write; (6) FUTURE is user_version>42 or an unsupported epoch/min-max range; fail state-dependent startup before either initializer, SessionDB, backup/reset, queue recovery, or export that assumes the current schema. After HUMAN selection, all consumers receive the frozen composition mode and open the already initialized v42 database; SessionDB must not independently redispatch it as legacy. Fresh default therefore means automatic HUMAN composition only for the approved genuinely fresh lane, persistence of that choice across restart through the bootstrap/epoch markers, and never an on-first-request upgrade of an existing or reset legacy userdata directory.
findings.root_cause: The plan names fresh, legacy, and future outcomes but does not assign a single pre-side-effect epoch classifier and initializer owner in lifespan. Existing composition has two legacy initialization calls and leaves human initialization to a later store method, so startup order—not the frozen data-format contract—currently decides the epoch.

findings.evidence: The finding is confirmed and refined. The established authority pattern is LocalAuthSnapshotProvider.current_snapshot() -> validate_auth_snapshot() -> HumanIdentity.identity_namespace_hash, with CompanionControlIngress._identity() comparing any supplied snapshot to the trusted snapshot and ValidatedLocalMemoryIdentityAuthority.bind() deriving actor identity rather than accepting it. The reused stores are not themselves a public trust boundary: HumanMemoryProgramStore.initialize_subject/open_primary_conversation use caller subject; append_evidence uses envelope.subject; CanonicalTaskScopeStore.create_task_scope uses caller subject, append_host_event/create_checkpoint/rebuild_projection have no subject argument, apply_mutation_plan only compares its embedded subject to the scope row, and _verify_refs_tx checks evidence_id/hash but not evidence subject or primary; TaskWorkspaceBindingStore accepts subject/run/scope-bearing DTOs, while current_receipt(task_scope_id) has no subject check. The required facade matrix is: primary.open — Host derives subject; payload may contain only requested primary ID/idempotency metadata; resolved primary.subject must equal Host subject and an exact requested ID must match. evidence.append — Host derives subject; payload supplies the frozen sanitized envelope/receipt; envelope.subject and receipt.subject must equal Host subject, their evidence/run/source/envelope/receipt hashes must agree, primary_conversation_id must be the Host subject's writable primary, and any referenced durable Run must belong to that subject. task_scope.create — Host derives subject; payload supplies scope ID, title, and idempotency key; persisted scope owner is always Host subject. task_scope.append_event/mutate/checkpoint/rebuild — Host derives subject; payload supplies exact scope/revision/event/plan/metadata; before every read or write the canonical scope.subject must equal Host subject; every evidence ref must resolve by ID plus hash plus subject plus Host primary, and every run-bearing ref must resolve to the same subject and compatible scope. search — Host derives subject and computes allowed scope IDs from canonical ownership plus any durable permission relation; payload supplies query, cursor, and bounds only and may not supply subject or allowed IDs; authorization relation is applied before MATCH/rank/snippet. open_exact — Host derives subject; payload supplies exact scope ID, expected source revision, page selectors, and bounded live probe; the scope must be in the Host-computed authorized set and the revision must match; it must not mutate cursor, binding, or grants. binding.manual_append — Host derives subject; payload supplies proposal/root/idempotency and signed interaction evidence; embedded subject must equal Host subject, scope owner and evidence must match it, run must be the current same-subject/same-scope Run, and the Host-issued authorization decision—not a payload flag—is authority. binding.auto_append — Host derives subject and loads the durable current Run snapshot; payload may select exact run/scope and propose a root but may not choose mode, subject, run revision, binding revision, context snapshot/revision/hash, configuration revision, or authority receipt; all run/scope/binding/context/config fields must match the Host-issued snapshot. queue.enqueue — Host derives subject; payload supplies idempotency, turn content, exact optional scope selector, and committed primary evidence ref; evidence must match Host subject/primary/hash, scope must be owned by Host subject, and any pre-existing run reference must be compatible; the queue row freezes this lineage before acknowledgement. queue.claim/settle — worker-internal only, not a caller-selectable public subject operation; Host selects the oldest eligible durable row, derives subject/scope/evidence from it, transactionally enforces the one-foreground-Run constraint, rejects background worker kinds, and settles only the claimed run generation. control — Host derives subject; payload supplies request ID, exact run ID, pause/stop/cancel kind, and reason; Host loads the current Run, verifies run.subject equals Host subject and active generation, then records immediate control outside normal FIFO. audit.refs — Host derives subject; payload supplies exact IDs and pagination bounds; every returned projection/search/checkpoint/binding/run/recovery receipt must trace to a Host-owned scope or primary and immutable hashes, with no arbitrary table/path selector. recovery/emergency-export — capability is owned by trusted Host lifecycle, not payload identity; per-subject material is restricted to Host-derived subject, payload contains only bounded action/idempotency/export options, and it cannot choose subject, database path, raw table, epoch, or min/max compatibility. The legacy CRUD fence must be a shared guard returning human_memory_primary_authority_immutable before any SQL write, handoff read, peer remap, workflow cancellation, or success event at these entries: project_protocol session_create and its SessionCreationService.create_conversation_session boundary, including source/requested/generated IDs; the chat new-session branch in backend/main.py around 15279 and its post-create remap around 15448; SessionDB.create_session and ensure_session for direct/internal creation; session_messages_load around 14201 before _remap_chat_peer_group as the effective public switch; every externally reachable _remap_chat_peer_group call after resolving its target; session_rename before SessionDB.set_session_title plus the set_session_title boundary; session_delete before SessionCreationService.mark_deleted or SessionDB.clear plus both mutation boundaries. Current delete/rename handlers swallow exceptions into ok=false, so the stable code must be carried in the response. memory_clear is not a separate Session CRUD authority, but if its backing store reaches SessionDB.clear the shared clear guard must still reject the primary.
findings.root_cause: The plan lists facade verbs without defining which fields are Host-derived, which payload fields are selectors only, or the mandatory subject-to-primary-to-scope-to-evidence-to-run-to-binding/context joins. Reused stores validate internal DTO consistency but intentionally do not authenticate callers, and legacy mutation handlers lack a common primary-authority fence.

conclusion.summary: Both parent findings remain open. Static composition proves the fresh epoch can currently be preempted by legacy initialization, and the reused stores cannot serve directly as public authorization boundaries. The review supplies an executable epoch dispatch state machine, fresh-default semantics, complete facade authority/lineage matrix, and the concrete legacy CRUD fence surface without expanding S5, S6, legacy migration, or multi-agent scope.
